new_symbol_range_suggestions.DeltaF_soft: positive and of order the experimentally sampled DeltaF range; choose DeltaF_soft > 0 so the barrier-dependent softening grows with DeltaF at low-to-moderate barriers and saturates for DeltaF >> DeltaF_soft

derivation_notes: The parent assumed the heat-capacity-induced softening term is independent of barrier scale. Here the same softening channel is retained but multiplied by a saturating barrier-shape factor 1 + DeltaF/(DeltaF + DeltaF_soft), representing broader or more anharmonic transition regions for larger barriers without introducing a new input.
change_summary: The effective barrier softening now depends nonlinearly on DeltaF through a finite saturating factor, so temperature curvature in k(T) is no longer shared across all barrier heights. This is a law refinement of the activated-rate mapping itself, not just a re-interpretation of parameters.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The heat-capacity-induced softening term enters the effective activation free energy independently of the reference barrier height DeltaF.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Barrier-shape heterogeneity makes the temperature-driven reduction of the effective barrier increase with barrier height and then saturate at large DeltaF.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent in the limit DeltaF_soft -> oo, where DeltaF/(DeltaF + DeltaF_soft) -> 0 and the barrier-dependent enhancement disappears.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed nu, xi_env, and DeltaF, temperature changes the rate through one effective activation exponent with a single heat-capacity-softening saturation scale T_sat, so log k versus 1/T has one shared curvature pattern for all barrier heights.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same activated-rate structure but relax the assumption that the same temperature-softened barrier shape controls all barrier heights linearly; allow barrier softening to depend on the barrier scale itself, so temperature-induced reduction of the effective barrier grows nonlinearly with DeltaF.
response_change.observable_effect: When T is varied at two fixed barrier heights, the higher-barrier case shows disproportionately stronger upward bending of k(T) than the lower-barrier case, beyond a simple vertical shift in log k that the parent can produce.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable for positive DeltaF with appreciable variation across DeltaF and moderate temperatures where C_act*T**2/(T + T_sat) is a non-negligible fraction of DeltaF but the rare-event regime still holds, so neither pure Arrhenius behavior nor near-barrierless saturation dominates.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying T at several DeltaF values reveals that temperature curvature is not shared across barriers; in holdout, the same barrier-dependent curvature persists at larger or intermediate DeltaF without changing mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the barrier dependence of softening is taken to zero, so the effective softening becomes independent of DeltaF and only the current single-scale temperature correction remains.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Barrier-height-dependent thermal softening with finite saturation
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Barrier-shape heterogeneity: systems with larger reference free-energy barriers can also have broader or more anharmonic transition-state regions, making the temperature-driven softening of the effective barrier itself depend on DeltaF.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a saturating DeltaF-T interaction inside the activation exponent and transmission factor, changing curvature across barrier groups rather than merely rescaling all curves or shifting them vertically.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The heat-capacity-induced softening term enters the effective activation free energy independently of the reference barrier height DeltaF.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The heat-capacity-induced softening is enhanced by barrier height through a finite saturating barrier-shape factor, so larger barriers experience stronger thermal curvature up to saturation.
evolution_contract.after_fragment: nu*exp(-(DeltaF - S_act*T - C_act*T**2*(1 + DeltaF/(DeltaF + DeltaF_soft))/(T + T_sat))/T)/(1 + (xi_env/T)*exp(-(C_act*T**2*(1 + DeltaF/(DeltaF + DeltaF_soft))/(T + T_sat))/T))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Take DeltaF_soft -> oo, which makes 1 + DeltaF/(DeltaF + DeltaF_soft) -> 1 and exactly recovers the parent expression.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed nu and xi_env, sweeping T for multiple positive DeltaF values no longer yields approximately shifted copies of one common thermal-curvature profile. Instead, the slope and upward bending of log k versus 1/T strengthen systematically with DeltaF over the regime where the softening term is visible but activation remains rare.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because in the parent DeltaF enters mainly as an additive barrier loading while the entire temperature-softening curvature is shared across all barriers through one common C_act*T**2/(T + T_sat) term. Retuning C_act, T_sat, S_act, or xi_env can move that shared curvature for all DeltaF at once, but cannot make higher-DeltaF cases bend more strongly with T than lower-DeltaF cases beyond a mostly vertical shift.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable for positive DeltaF with appreciable variation across DeltaF and moderate temperatures where C_act*T**2/(T + T_sat) is a non-negligible fraction of DeltaF but the rare-event regime still holds, so neither pure Arrhenius behavior nor near-barrierless saturation dominates.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying T at several DeltaF values reveals that temperature curvature is not shared across barriers; in holdout, the same barrier-dependent curvature persists at larger or intermediate DeltaF without changing mechanism.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the barrier dependence of softening is taken to zero, so the effective softening becomes independent of DeltaF and only the current single-scale temperature correction remains.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes the same temperature-softening correction applies additively to every barrier height, so changing DeltaF mainly shifts the exponent without changing how thermal curvature itself depends on barrier scale.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The heat-capacity-induced softening term enters the effective activation free energy independently of the reference barrier height DeltaF.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Barrier-shape heterogeneity: systems with larger reference free-energy barriers can also have broader or more anharmonic transition-state regions, making the temperature-driven softening of the effective barrier itself depend on DeltaF.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: at fixed nu and xi_env, DeltaF enters essentially as a single exponential loading while the temperature-dependent softening term C_act*T**2/(T + T_sat) is shared across all barriers, so different DeltaF curves are close to shifted versions of one another in thermal coordinates. The proposed child changes the target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary interpretation, by making the temperature curvature of k depend on DeltaF. Distinguishing condition: vary T while holding nu and xi_env fixed, and compare two or more positive DeltaF values in a regime where the softening term is visible but does not eliminate activation. Then the parent with one shared parameter set can only change barrier-height dependence mostly through a vertical/overall exponential shift, whereas the child predicts that the slope and curvature of k(T) differ systematically with DeltaF. This is scientifically admissible when barrier shape correlates with barrier height, a common refinement beyond idealized fixed-shape transition-state theory. Limitation: if the accessible data stay in a very low-T regime where the softening term is negligible relative to DeltaF for all cases, the contrast collapses and the parent is effectively recovered.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: Consider rare thermally activated transitions between two metastable macrostates separated by a free-energy barrier. Independent equilibrium preparations vary the barrier height, bath temperature, and microscopic attempt frequency, while the bath remains unchanged by each event. The target is the mean transition rate in the dilute-event regime. Collective recrossing and depletion of the initial macrostate are excluded from the baseline response.
